chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Abd Allah ibn Maymun from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) from his father (peace be upon him) said:

The Zakat al-Fitr is a sa' of dates, or a sa' of raisins, or a sa' of barley, or a sa' of aqit, for every person, free or slave, young or old. And there is no blame on one who cannot find what to give in charity.

key_terms.زَكَاةُ الْفِطْرَةِ: Zakat al-Fitr (the alms-tax given at the end of Ramadan)
key_terms.صَاعٌ: A sa' (a traditional unit of volume measurement)

ai.seo_question: What are the valid items and amounts for Zakat al-Fitr in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar specifies the canonical measures for Zakat al-Fitr, listing dates, raisins, barley, and aqit (dried curds) as valid forms of payment. It underscores the universality of the obligation across all demographics—free, slave, male, female, child, and adult—while providing a practical exemption for those lacking the financial means, reflecting the juristic principle of ease in worship.
